title: The Reformed admit infused habits; the charge against them is unjust
source_text: XLVII. Deinde planum est ex iis quae fuerunt ante exposita, Scholae Reformatae Doctores admittere virtutes quasdam divinitus infusas, & dona quaedam gratiae salvificae, quae sint in anima per modum habitus & qualitatis permanentis: adeoque immerito a Theologis Romanae communionis illis imputari, quod negent dari gratiam aliquam habitualem, & quae sit qualitas in anima inhaerens; cum istud ab Ecclesiae Reformatae Doctoribus vel nullis, vel paucis negetur.
pass_a_gloss: XLVII. Next it is plain from those things which were set out before, that the Doctors of the Reformed School admit certain virtues divinely infused, and certain gifts of saving grace, which are in the soul by way of habit and permanent quality: and so it is undeservedly imputed to them by the Theologians of the Roman communion, that they deny that there is given some habitual grace, and which is a quality inhering in the soul; since that is denied by either none, or few of the Doctors of the Reformed Church.
pass_b_english: Thesis XLVII. Next, it is clear from what was set out earlier that the doctors of the Reformed school admit certain divinely infused virtues and certain gifts of saving grace that exist in the soul as a habit and permanent quality.

So the theologians of the Roman communion unjustly charge them with denying that there is any habitual grace that is a quality inhering in the soul, since few or none of the doctors of the Reformed Church deny it.
